palette.notes: Colour count not discussed; drop shadows are drawn as separate tile layers or baked in when there is room.

lighting: Implied by layered drop shadows under trees, rocks and cliffs rather than shading on the sprites.
silhouette: Tiny hero on 8x8 tiles (the author's usual is 16x16 tiles and 16x32 characters): only a few cues survive, shoulder pads and flaming red hair, and the viewer fills in the rest.

motion.timing: Each frame can only shift by one pixel, so a full stride takes just a few frames; extra frames add little. No durations given.

texture: Layered tiles: dirt, grass, shadows, trees and rocks, cliffs with more shadows on top; detail kept low on purpose.
camera: Fixed 4:3 play area with UI in the margins, suggested because widescreen at this scale looks chunky.

acting.acts: A one- or two-pixel shift reads as a head turn or a change in posture; that tiny change is the acting.
acting.depth: Depth from layer order and drop shadows; large enemies split into layered pieces animated separately.

techniques: keep only 2-3 identity cues at tiny sizes (hair colour, shoulder pads)
1-2 px shift for a head turn or posture change
few-frame walk: one pixel per frame
drop shadows as a separate layer
split big figures into layered parts
stop detailing early; leave gaps for the viewer
feel: 2 identity cues + 1 px head turns + layered shadows = charm from what you leave out
for_fred: When Fred appears small in the background, shrink him to just his identity cues (orange body, tail fin shape) and act with 1-2 px shifts: a head turn toward the presenter, a tiny bob, then out. Don't draw a detailed mini-Fred; the background cameo should read from silhouette and colour alone.
